subject: Game Theory
title: Betrayal Aversion
description: Learn Betrayal Aversion in one minute.

hook.text: Losing $100 to a scammer hurts more than losing $100 to bad luck—even though the loss is identical.

buildup.text: Betrayal aversion means people feel extra pain when losses result from someone breaking trust intentionally.

discovery.text: Experiments show people pay more to avoid human betrayal than random loss—even when probabilities are the same.

twist.text: This makes people over-cautious after betrayal: they avoid cooperation entirely, even with trustworthy partners.

climax.text: Betrayal aversion explains why scandals devastate brands. The VW emissions fraud cost far more than the fine.

punchline.text: Betrayal scars deeper than bad luck.

quiz.question: Why does betrayal hurt more than equivalent random loss?
options: Humans feel extra pain from intentional trust violations
